promptConfig.description: whether the user maintained their morning fast
promptConfig.scale: boolean — true if the fast was maintained, false if the fast was broken
notes: Only consider items consumed between midnight and noon (00:00-12:00).
Afternoon and evening eating does NOT affect this score — ignore it entirely.
Return true if no food or caloric intake occurred outside the fasting window.
Non-caloric items, medications, supplements, and antacids (e.g. Rennie, ibuprofen, water, black coffee, plain tea) do NOT break the fast — treat intake of these items as true.
Only evaluate as false if caloric intake exceeds 10 kcal or includes an actual meal or snack during the fasting window.

promptConfig.description: the intensity of afternoon snacking activity
promptConfig.scale: 0.0 = no snacking at all, 1.0 = very frequent or heavy snacking
integer count — number of caffeinated drinks consumed (cups of coffee, lungo, espresso shots, energy drinks, etc.)
notes: For each time window, count the total number of caffeinated drink items consumed.
Return 0 if none are found, or null if there is genuinely not enough data to determine.

promptConfig.description: the intensity of added sugar consumption
promptConfig.scale: 0.0 = no added sugar consumed, 1.0 = very high added sugar consumption (frequent sugary foods or drinks)
notes: Consider both food and drink sources of added sugar.
Natural sugars in whole fruits should weigh less heavily than refined or added sugars.

promptConfig.scale: integer — estimated total calories consumed within the time window, based on the described food and drink items
notes: Estimate calories using typical caloric values for the foods and drinks described.
Return null if there is genuinely not enough information to make a reasonable estimate.
